problem_text:
A regional power grid operator must inspect ten substations scattered across a service territory.  

The travel times between substations, measured in minutes, are as follows:  
* Substation Alpha to Beta: 146.7 minutes  
* Alpha to Gamma: 10.2 minutes  
* Alpha to Delta: 172.2 minutes  
* Alpha to Epsilon: 60.3 minutes  
* Alpha to Zeta: 64.3 minutes  
* Alpha to Eta: 125.3 minutes  
* Alpha to Theta: 141.4 minutes  
* Alpha to Iota: 154.3 minutes  
* Alpha to Kappa: 91.0 minutes  
* Beta to Gamma: 154.8 minutes  
* Beta to Delta: 30.4 minutes  
* Beta to Epsilon: 93.0 minutes  
* Beta to Zeta: 174.8 minutes  
* Beta to Eta: 189.8 minutes  
* Beta to Theta: 108.1 minutes  
* Beta to Iota: 189.1 minutes  
* Beta to Kappa: 94.8 minutes  
* Gamma to Delta: 180.9 minutes  
* Gamma to Epsilon: 70.1 minutes  
* Gamma to Zeta: 68.9 minutes  
* Gamma to Eta: 132.1 minutes  
* Gamma to Theta: 151.5 minutes  
* Gamma to Iota: 162.3 minutes  
* Gamma to Kappa: 101.2 minutes  
* Delta to Epsilon: 115.0 minutes  
* Delta to Zeta: 193.1 minutes  
* Delta to Eta: 198.6 minutes  
* Delta to Theta: 106.2 minutes  
* Delta to Iota: 192.0 minutes  
* Delta to Kappa: 107.6 minutes  
* Epsilon to Zeta: 83.5 minutes  
* Epsilon to Eta: 116.0 minutes  
* Epsilon to Theta: 89.0 minutes  
* Epsilon to Iota: 131.3 minutes  
* Epsilon to Kappa: 38.3 minutes  
* Zeta to Eta: 66.5 minutes  
* Zeta to Theta: 123.8 minutes  
* Zeta to Iota: 101.5 minutes  
* Zeta to Kappa: 87.8 minutes  
* Eta to Theta: 101.2 minutes  
* Eta to Iota: 38.3 minutes  
* Eta to Kappa: 95.5 minutes  
* Theta to Iota: 86.8 minutes  
* Theta to Kappa: 51.4 minutes  
* Iota to Kappa: 101.3 minutes  

The objective is to determine the inspection circuit of minimal total duration that visits every substation precisely once and concludes at the initial substation.
